newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL short-term rates rise on bids, some fund flow.
newsitem.headline: KL short-term rates rise on bids, some fund flow.

text.p: Short-term interbank rates rose on bids by small finance houses and perception of tightness due to outflow of 500 million ringgit from the system, dealers said.
"The rates are up on bids by not-so-good names," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank, referring to small finance houses.
Perceived as higher risk borrowers, the smaller houses have to borrow funds at higher levels than the larger banks and finance firms.
Other dealers said today's payment for 500 million ringgit 30-day Bank Negara bills led to some liquidity tightness.
Dealers said one-week interbank rate was quoted at 7.30/40 percent from 6.80/7.00 on Tuesday.
Two-week money was at 7.30/40 percent from 7.20/25 and three-week at 7.25/30 from 7.20/30.

They said the rates were unlikely to trade much higher as funds generally remain easily available due to inflow of overseas money. Malaysia's surging stockmarket and high interest rates continue to attract offshore funds.
Some dealers said they expect the overnight rate to trade higher than Tuesday's close of 5.60 percent, based on the rise of short-term rates.
One-month rate was at 7.30/35 percent from 7.20/25 previously. The three-month, six-month and one-year were unchanged at 7.30/35 percent.
